rv.q: This isn't a major musical to rival South Pacific but in a West End awash with shows for kids and kidults it dares to speak to our inner grown-up about frustrated yearning, fleeting romance and pluck.
From Here to Eternity is hard to love but easy to like.
Yet what really allows the show to seem simply too long rather than an eternity is an unusually varied and tune-packed score.
For all the show's many defects, though, you come away impressed by its seriousness of purpose.
Until that point, the overriding sense is of a musical based on skilled professionalism rather than expressive need.
From Here to Eternity aspires to be both gritty and erotic, yet in the end seems sprawling and underpowered.

It's a commendably ambitious work that makes a refreshing addition to the West End menu.
There are, in fact, many reasons to see this show.
Sir Tim's work is first out of the stocks, and let me say straight away that I like it.

cn.t: A professionally crafted but ultimately underwhelming musical that returns Tim Rice to the West End after 13 years. Critics praise its ambition and return to Jones's unexpurgated novel, but question whether music adds much to the familiar story.
